back: A resistive force on an object moving through a fluid, acting opposite to its velocity relative to the fluid; increases with speed.
The constant velocity reached when the resistive forces (and upthrust) balance the driving force or weight, so the resultant force is zero.

front: Acceleration of a falling object with air resistance
back: Starts at g and decreases to zero as drag increases with speed.

front: v-t graph for reaching terminal velocity
back: A curve starting with gradient g whose gradient falls until the graph is horizontal.

front: What happens when a parachute opens?
back: Drag exceeds weight, so the parachutist decelerates (still moving down) to a lower terminal velocity.
Reached when the maximum driving force equals the total resistive force.
Drag increases with speed (roughly ∝ v at low speed in viscous fluids, ∝ v² for fast objects in air), with area and with fluid density; it depends on shape.
Friction and drag transfer kinetic energy to internal energy (heating).
